title: SDK circuit breakers and fallbacks — runloop notes
body:
Purpose:
A focused working note for the SDK team: define lightweight client-side circuit-breaker + fallback behavior that is trivial for integrators to opt into, easy to reason about during outages, and compatible with Redwood’s routing/fallback model.

Context / motivation:
- We see a handful of customer apps that treat any upstream 5xx or timeout as a hard failure and surface raw errors to end-users. That kills UX during transient infra events.
- Redwood server-side already supports model-level fallback routing (eg: m1 -> m1-quant -> m2). But client SDKs can improve fast-fail, reduce retry storms, and present graceful UX while server-side runbooks are triggered.
- Goal: default SDK behavior that is safe for web/mobile apps and flexible for power users. Should minimize surprises and be observable.

Non-goals:
- Replace server-side fallback orchestration.
- Create a full stateful circuit-breaker library — keep it small and stateless where possible.

High-level requirements (MVP):
1) Fast-fail for downstream latency spikes: SDK should surface a short client-side timeout (T_client) by default to avoid keeping UI blocked and to assist bulkheads.
2) Soft-circuit: after N_fast_fails within window W, mark endpoint as degraded for D seconds and switch to an immediate fallback mode (return a cached value, use a cheaper/approximate model requested by server, or return a client-level stub).
3) Retry policy: limited, jittered, and idempotency-aware. Default: 1 retry on network errors only, 200–500ms jittered backoff.
4) Observability: counters for fast_fail, soft_open, retries, fallbacks_used, and reason tags (timeout/5xx/network). These should be emitted as SDK metrics and as structured logs.
5) Config surface: minimal — allow clients to override thresholds and supply a fallback callback. Keep defaults conservative.

Proposed default config (suggested values):
- T_client = 2s (overall request timeout)
- N_fast_fails = 3
- W = 60s window
- D = 30s degrade period
- retry_policy = { attempts: 1, base_delay_ms: 120, jitter: 0.3 }  // describe in docs rather than structured object
- fallback_mode default = "throw-with-cause"; optional values: "return-stub", "use-cache", "call-fallback-model"

Fallback hook semantics (SDK API suggestion):
- onFallback(ctx, reason) -> returns either: fallbackValue (sync) OR promise of fallbackValue OR throw to propagate original error.
- The SDK invokes onFallback only when soft-circuit is active OR final attempt fails.
- Example patterns for integrator: show a cached response, render a degraded UX (skeleton), or trigger a local NLU fallback.

Failure modes and edge cases:
- Retry storms: avoid retrying on server 429/503 unless Retry-After present and client respects it.
- Long polling and streaming: circuit logic should ignore streaming reads (these are separate flows). For streaming, provide a per-chunk timeout instead.
- Non-idempotent requests: do not retry by default. Provide explicit opt-in parameter (safeRetries: true) for idempotent endpoints only.
- Cold-start: if the app launches and no cache/fallback exists, soft-circuit should prefer immediate no-op stub rather than blocking UI. Document tradeoffs.

Runloop checklist for SDK implementers (developer checklist):
- [ ] Implement counters for consecutive failures and sliding-window counts.
- [ ] Expose surface to read circuit state for telemetry (closed, half-open, open).
- [ ] Hook into existing telemetry pipeline: metric names prefixed sdk.resilience.* with tags: sdk_lang, client_version, route, reason.
- [ ] Add a user-configurable onFallback callback with examples in README.
- [ ] Unit tests for: timeout triggers, retry jitter, open/close transitions, fallback callback invocation.
- [ ] E2E smoke: simulate server 500 bursts and verify fallback used and metrics emitted.

Quickstart for integrators (developer-facing):
- JS SDK example (pseudocode):

  const client = RedwoodSDK({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, timeoutMs: 2000, fallback: (ctx, reason) => {
    // simple cache fallback
    const cached = localCache.get(ctx.hash);
    if (cached) return cached;
    return { text: "We're having trouble — showing cached summary" };
  }});

  try {
    const resp = await client.generate(prompt);
    render(resp.text);
  } catch (err) {
    // fallback was either returned or throw occurred -> show error banner
    showBanner("Temporary issue — please try again");
  }

Operational notes for SRE/Support:
- Map SDK metric sdk.resilience.soft_open -> SLO alert threshold (eg: >2% of requests per minute for >5m).
- Dashboard: ratio of fallbacks_used / total_requests, average TTFB for fallback vs normal path.
- When investigating, correlate with server-side routing fallbacks and region capacity events.

Docs & UX copy (short snippets for README):
- "Resilience defaults: the SDK will fast-fail brief outages and offer a simple hook for graceful fallbacks. You can tweak thresholds or provide your own fallback handler. These defaults are intentionally conservative to protect user experience and limit retry storms."

Open questions / tradeoffs to resolve:
- Should we allow server to advertise suggested T_client values per-route via header? (pro: dynamic tuning; con: complexity & trust)
- What is the canonical SDK metric taxonomy? We'll propose concrete names in follow-up PR.
- Should the SDK attempt a background refresh while serving a cached fallback? (nice UX but complicates concurrency/semantics)
- Do we provide a built-in 'fallback-model' shim that calls Redwood's low-cost variant automatically? How to surface billing/consent?

Next steps (short-term):
1) Proto implementation in JS and Rust SDKs: basic circuit counters + onFallback hook. Owner: Miguel. ETA: 2025-02-18.
2) Add unit/e2e tests and a small smoke harness that can simulate the three failure profiles (timeout, 5xx burst, 429 backoff). Owner: Samir. ETA: 2025-02-28.
3) Draft README quickstart and a short explainer snippet for Console docs. Owner: Aisha. ETA: 2025-03-04.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Keep public API surface tiny: toggles for timeoutMs, maxConsecutiveFails, onFallback. Everything else internal.
- Consider a 'dev-mode' that prints state transitions to console to aid debugging.
- Remember mobile environments: lower default T_client for poor networks (maybe 1.2s). Could be platform override.

Relevant links / references to review before implementation:
- RFC: client-retries-and-idempotency (Confluence)
- Git PR: sdk-js-resilience-experiments (linked above)
- Support ticket queue: many small customer reports of UI freeze during short 503 bursts (support-#2311)
